supplierKPIs.description: Fees charged by employer: illegal and unethical
Inaccurate / misleading / poor information about job: serious, deceptive mis-information
Proper legal documents not provided to workers
remediation_sp_recommendation: Issue SSO cards to all affected workers within 30 days and confirm receipt with each worker
Reconcile and disclose to workers all past SSO contributions deducted from their wages, in Burmese
supplierKPIs.worker_issue_summary: The workers reported that they have still not been provided with their social security (SSO) cards, although the business has been deducting the SSO contribution monthly from their salaries for months. The workers consent to their names being shared with their employer, to remediate this issue for them asap.
supplierKPIs.issara_action: We conveyed this information to the head of HR via a phone call and noted that the workers should have their cards in-hand as per the law.
supplierKPIs.supplier_action: The head of HR said she would investigate what the cause of the delay has been in giving the cards to the workers. She explained that if the workers needed to visit the hospital, they should still be able to do so. But she also agreed that the workers should have their cards in-hand.

supplierKPIs.description: Fees charged by upstream/village-level broker: legal but not ethical
Inaccurate / misleading / poor information about job: minor miscommunication
remediation_sp_recommendation: The Management Service Agreement and Code of Conduct should be clearly communicated and reinforced with all suppliers to ensure full understanding and compliance. For future recruitment processes, suppliers should engage directly with the source recruiter to maintain transparency and proper oversight. Additionally, the Service Provider should require the engagement of Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) in the source country to help monitor recruitment practices and minimize potential risks starting from the first miles.

supplierKPIs.description: Fees charged by recruitment agency: illegal and unethical
remediation_sp_recommendation: The message should be reinforced with all suppliers, and verification should be conducted to ensure that all suppliers provide employment contracts in languages that workers can clearly understand. If translation support for workers' contracts is required, Issara Institute is available to assist in providing accurate translations. In addition, the Management Service Agreement between suppliers and the SP should be clearly explained to suppliers. All requirements and key terms should be communicated in languages that are familiar and easily understood by the suppliers to ensure full comprehension and compliance.
